extracted.intended_audience: predoctoral applicants to NIA F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research fellowship (and mentors/institutional grant administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling an NIA F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research fellowship application (predoctoral F99 phase and K00 transition) including required SF424/PHS components, human subjects protections, training plans, sponsor statements, and institutional resource descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) APPLICATION FOR FEDERAL ASSISTANCE — Required Forms/Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the SF424 (R&R) application form fields (Type of Submission; Date Submitted; Federal Identifier; Applicant Information; Employer Identification Number (EIN/TIN); Type of Applicant; Type of Application; Authorized Representative signature and date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accurate applicant/legal name and contact, organizational DUNS, department, addresses, authorized representative signature certifying compliance with assurances and certifications. Ensure correct Type of Application (New/Resubmission/Continuation/etc.) and completion of submission-type checkboxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project/Performance Site Location(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Project/Performance Site primary location and any additional locations, including congressional district for the performance site(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List organization name, DUNS, street, city/state/zip, and project/performance site congressional district (e.g., CA-037).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Other Project Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer key project information questions: Are human subjects involved? Is the project exempt? Are vertebrate animals used? Is proprietary/privileged information included? Environmental impact? Historic place designation? International activities? Provide attachment filenames for summary, narrative, references, facilities, equipment, and other attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, indicate exemption status or IRB pending/approval and provide Human Subjects Assurance Number. Attach Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Bibliography & References, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, and other required documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise Project Summary/Abstract describing aims, significance, and study scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach as a separate file (e.g., 04__Project_Summary1016533226.pdf). The summary should clearly state the research question, methods, datasets, and intended outcomes for the proposed F99/K00 work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a public-health-relevance narrative describing how the proposed work addresses important problems (e.g., social isolation and cognitive health in older adults) and the potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the Project Narrative file (e.g., 05__Project_Narrative1016533227.pdf) that frames broader significance and relevance to aging research and intended translational impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Include full Bibliography & References Cited documenting prior work and supporting literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach references (e.g., 06__References_Cited1016533157.pdf); include citations supporting background, methods, measures, and rationale (as in the provided references list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional resources, research space, IT infrastructure, data storage, core centers, and administrative support available to the applicant and project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed Facilities & Other Resources document (example: USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work description), including dedicated research space, secure data storage, video conferencing, software (SAS, NVivo), IT support, biostatistical and database staff, research administration support (CRAs), and access to institutional systems (Cayuse, TARA, iStar, disClose, Sophia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment available for the project or state that there is no major equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach an equipment file (e.g., No_Major_Equipment_Doc1016533159.pdf) specifying available instruments, computing resources, imaging or lab equipment if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Attachments / Certification Letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Include additional required attachments such as certification letters, cover letter, or institutional assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach Certification_Letter and Cover Letter files (e.g., Certification_Letter_Kexin_Yu_Oct_191016533214.pdf, 02_cover_letter1016533154.pdf). Ensure MIME types and file names are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person
rubrics_metrics.description: List the PD/PI and all senior/key personnel, their roles, affiliations, and contributions to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include names, role categories (PD/PI, Co-Sponsor, Sponsor, Other), institutional affiliations, and specify who is responsible for which aspects of the project (e.g., Kexin Yu PD/PI; co-sponsors and sponsor named).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Required Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the PHS Fellowship Supplemental components: Applicant's Background and Goals for Fellowship Training; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Respective Contributions; Selection of Sponsor and Institution; Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research; Sponsor and Co-Sponsor Statements; Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants; Description of Institutional Environment and Commitment to Training; PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the fellowship-specific application materials as separate attachments/sections reflecting each required heading; the Table of Contents lists expected page/attachment locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Background and Goals for Fellowship Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the applicant's prior training/background and specific career and training goals for the fellowship period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the F99/K00 will complete dissertation research and prepare the applicant for postdoctoral training in aging research; demonstrate fit between goals and proposed training activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a succinct Specific Aims page articulating the primary aims/hypotheses to be tested during the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state aims for the F99 dissertation work and how these link to planned K00 postdoctoral objectives; be concise and focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the research approach, including study design, data sources (e.g., NHATS waves 5–8, I-CONECT), analytic methods (e.g., latent growth curve modeling), and proposed qualitative components (focus groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe secondary quantitative analyses and primary qualitative methods, sample sizes (e.g., NHATS n=8,334; I-CONECT recruitment goals), mixed-methods integration, statistical considerations, and how results will inform intervention development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respective Contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the respective contributions of the applicant, sponsor, co-sponsors, and collaborators to the proposed training and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail mentoring plan, roles of key personnel (e.g., who will lead analyses, supervise focus groups), and how each contributor will support training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Sponsor and Institution / Sponsor and Co-Sponsor Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sponsor/co-sponsor statements confirming availability, mentorship commitment, institutional support, and resources for training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include written statements describing sponsor qualifications, proposed mentoring activities, time commitment, institutional commitment to the trainee, and letters of support from co-sponsors and relevant centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a plan for RCR training for the trainee during the fellowship period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain RCR coursework, workshops, or institutional requirements the fellow will complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach letters evidencing collaborator and consultant commitments and describing their roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should specify the nature of the collaboration, deliverables, and resources to be provided; include recruitment assistance commitments if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Institutional Environment and Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional environment, available centers/cores, and the institution's commitment to training the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of a supportive environment (examples: research centers, IT resources, training programs, dedicated research space, administrative support) and discuss how the environment will help the fellow meet training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information (General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full Human Subjects and Clinical Trials information: inclusion/enrollment reports, IRB status (pending/approved), whether the study is multi-site, whether an FDA-regulated intervention is used, and whether a DSMB will be appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include attachments for Protection of Human Subjects; if human subjects are involved, give Human Subjects Assurance Number, indicate IRB review status, and include enrollment demographic tables as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects — Human Subjects Involvement, Characteristics, and Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe human subjects involvement and study design (e.g., secondary analysis of NHATS waves 5–8; I-CONECT randomized trial; focus groups), sample sizes, inclusion criteria, and recruitment plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify that secondary data are de-identified (PI has no access to names in NHATS), details of I-CONECT recruitment goals (160 per site, 320 total), anticipated focus group numbers (two per site × 2 sites × ~8 participants each), and IRB submission plans for both primary and secondary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects — Study Procedures and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail study procedures (quantitative and qualitative), interventions (e.g., video-chat intervention schedule), assessments (in-home visits, MRIs), recording of sessions, and data collection modalities (audio-video recordings, electronic pillboxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intervention dosing (e.g., 30 minutes/day, 4x/week for 6 months then 2x/week for maintenance), telephone check-ins, in-person assessments at baseline/6/12 months, and plans to record sessions for speech/language analysis; note who will have which procedures (e.g., MRIs only if safe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects — Potential Risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential risks to participants (minimal risk expected), confidentiality risks, discomfort from discussing social isolation, and risks related to data handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that data will be de-identified where possible, contact info stored separately, participants may decline to answer questions or withdraw, and describe transportation arrangements and compensation for focus group participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of Protection Against Risks — Informed Consent and Assent
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe informed consent procedures for primary data (focus groups) and note existing consent for parent studies (I-CONECT); explain how consent will be obtained and stored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain recruitment phone calls, provision of written informed consent prior to data collection, process for answering questions, assent capacity of individuals with MCI, storage of signed consent in locked file cabinets for required retention period, and conditions for waiver if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of Protection Against Risks — Protection Against Risk (Confidentiality and Data Security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe measures to protect confidentiality and secure data (password-protected files, separate storage of names and IDs, IRB training for staff, access limited to research team and Human Subjects Protection Program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe de-identification procedures, password protection, secure backups, destruction of original focus group summaries after analysis, IRB training and addition of staff to IRB records, and anonymized/aggregated dissemination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Benefits and Importance of Knowledge to be Gained
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain potential benefits to participants and the public, and importance of the knowledge (e.g., informing interventions, policy for aging-friendly communities, potential direct benefits from participation in interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how secondary analyses and trial results could inform interventions and policy, potential direct benefits from the I-CONECT intervention, and broader societal relevance due to population aging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (DSMP) / DSM Board Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Data and Safety Monitoring Plan and state whether a Data and Safety Monitoring Board will be appointed for the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate DSMP attachment and whether DSMB required; in this application the DSMP is included and the applicant indicates 'No' for DSMB appointment (or explain why DSMB is not planned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Structure of the Study Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the organizational structure of the study team, roles and responsibilities of investigators, research assistants, and collaborating site personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include coordination across multiple sites (if applicable), recruitment responsibilities (I-CONECT team at OHSU and UM helping recruit focus groups), who leads focus groups, note-taking/transcription roles, and oversight by PI and research staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Synopsis / Study Design and Outcome Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise protocol synopsis including brief summary, narrative study description, primary purpose, interventions, study phase, intervention model, masking, allocation, outcome measures (type, name, time frame, brief description), statistical design and power, subject participation duration, and dissemination plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Protocol Synopsis sections (4.1–4.7) and fill in Outcome Measures and Statistical Design & Power information; include justification if not an NIH-defined Phase III trial and specify dissemination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether key biological/chemical resources will be used and provide authentication procedures if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no key biological/chemical resources are used, state so explicitly (as in this application: 'No key biological and/or chemical resources will be used'). If they are used, provide authentication plans and documentation.
